---
title: "Set Identities"
---

This exercise is adapted from @Abbott2015.

::: {#exr-de-morgan-union name="De Morgan's law for unions" .exercise}
For a sequence of sets $(A_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$, show that

$$
\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)^c
=
\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i^c.
$$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

We show equality by a chain of biconditionals. For arbitrary $x$,

\begin{align*}
x \in \left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right)^c
&\iff x \notin \bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i \\
&\iff x \notin A_i \text{ for every } i\in\mathbb N \\
&\iff x \in A_i^c \text{ for every } i\in\mathbb N \\
&\iff x \in \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i^c.
\end{align*}
:::
:::

This elementwise proof establishes the identity directly.
